artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $A$ of integers, define the sumset $A+A=\{a+b : a,b\in A\}$ and the product set $A\cdot A=\{ab : a,b\in A\}$. Prove or disprove the following statement: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a constant $c=c(\varepsilon)>0$ such that for every finite set $A\subset\mathbb{Z}$,
\[ \max\{|A+A|,\ |A\cdot A|\} \;\geq\; c\,|A|^{2-\varepsilon}. \]
artifact.status_search_result: The Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture remains open. The best known lower bound for max(|A+A|, |A·A|) over the reals is of order |A|^(4/3 + c) for a small constant c (Rudnev–Stevens, improving Konyagin–Shkredov and Solymosi), far from the conjectured exponent 2−ε.

status_evidence.title: Erdős–Szemerédi theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture states max(|A+A|,|A·A|) ≥ |A|^{2-ε}; current best bound is approximately |A|^{4/3+c}.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open with best exponent about 4/3 plus a small constant.

status_evidence.title: An update on the sum-product problem (Rudnev–Stevens)
status_evidence.snippet: Improvement of the sum-product exponent over the reals up to 4/3 + 1/1509.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress only improves the exponent slightly beyond 4/3, far from 2−ε.
